01-constraint.w: STRK20 reaches the outside world through one primitive.
Two protocol rules shape everything downstream.
At most one external call per pool transaction.
And every token's balance must end at exactly zero.

02-consequence.w: Together they mean a private action is only as expressive as the single helper contract it calls.
Deploy and audit a swap helper.
That is why almost everything built on STRK20 today is a payment app: payments are the only thing you can ship without writing Cairo.

03-plan.w: Jalin is a router, not an application.
It ships no use case of its own.
It takes a plan instead of fixed parameters: a bounded list of steps, each naming a target, a selector, calldata, and the approvals it needs.
It runs them in order inside the single privacy invoke and enforces the floor the caller set on each output.

04-general.w: Any Starknet contract is a valid target and the calldata is free form.
That is what makes a bridge call, a DEX route, and a lending deposit the same object.
Composition moves inside the single invoke, where the protocol allows it.

05-safety.w: Free calldata sounds unsafe, so safety is carried by invariants in Cairo rather than by a whitelist.
The router holds nothing between transactions, and anything left on it is unreachable.
That is why each output can be credited its whole balance instead of a measured delta.

06-governor.w: The router holds no admin key.
Every parameter it reads belongs to a governor that moves only by a vote, and the page asks the router which governor that is rather than trusting a config file.

07-redeem.w: A vote stakes value privately and hands the voter a secret.
Until this week the contract could give that stake back and nothing could ask it to: redeem was written in Cairo, tested in Cairo, and reachable from no code at all.

08-mainnet.w: This runs on Starknet mainnet against the live pool.
Here is one of its transactions being checked against the chain right now.
The page reads the receipt and answers four questions.
Does it exist, did it succeed, did it touch the STRK20 pool, and did it run through our own contract.

09-hub.w: It reads a whole submission too, and beside its own verdict it shows the sprint hub's.
Every listed transaction counted, and the two agree.

This endpoint answers for any team's repository, not just ours: one team took a measurement from our documentation and caught a seven day window in their own code that would have closed in three hours.

10-services.w: Six issues on the sprint tracker asked where the proving service was while it had been answering the whole time.
So this page asks all three services on every load, including how far behind the chain note discovery is.
That number decides whether a note you just created is findable by its recipient yet.

11-close.w: One general router instead of a new contract per interaction.
Cairo tests, a published SDK, a threat model, and every claim on this page verifiable against mainnet.
To weave separate strands into one.
